evidence.text: The database analyzes bronze 常 as 巾 semantic plus 尚 phonetic, with a lower-body garment sense. It reports that 常 and 裳 were originally graphic variants for this sense; later 常 was used for frequent/regular meanings and 裳 retained the garment sense. Examples it names include the Zifan bell inscription and Warring States bamboo slips for clothing, and a bronze inscription for ‘custom/law’. It also reports historical mixing of 常 and 嘗. These are database reports; the inspected entry gives no artifact dates.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: The entry quotes the received Shuowen analysis ‘lower skirt; from 巾, 尚 phonetic’ and says 裳 is a variant with 衣. It reports that the 裳 form became usual for the clothing sense and 常 became dedicated to ‘frequently’. It separately lists rule/order, ordinary, lasting, regular, frequent, office title, and ancient length-unit senses, citing classical works. Those citations attest textual usage but the entry does not establish first-use dates for the senses.
evidence.title: 常 - Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

evidence.source: Academia Sinica, 漢字構形資料庫
evidence.text: The inspected page lists Chu manuscript, small seal, and Shuowen forms, and explicitly identifies lower 巾 as semantic and 尚 as phonetic. Its page text did not provide a textual sequence of graphic changes or accessible image descriptions sufficient to compare individual forms.
evidence.title: 漢字「常」：字形演變

evidence.source: Wiktionary, 常 entry (tables citing named reconstruction systems)
evidence.text: The entry gives Mandarin cháng (Pinyin), Cantonese soeng4 (Jyutping), Middle Chinese dzyang, and Zhengzhang Shangfang 2003 Old Chinese *djaŋ for 常. Its Baxter–Sagart 2014 table instead gives *[d]aŋ. In the Zhengzhang table 常 is assigned phonetic component 尚. These are system-specific reconstructions, not direct records of ancient speech.
evidence.title: 常 - Wiktionary

evidence.source: Wiktionary, 尚 entry (tables citing named reconstruction systems)
evidence.text: The entry gives modern Mandarin shàng. For the level-tone reading it lists Middle Chinese dzyang and Zhengzhang Shangfang 2003 Old Chinese *djaŋ; for a departing-tone reading it lists Middle Chinese dzyangH and Zhengzhang *djaŋs. Compared with 常's level-tone *djaŋ in the same Zhengzhang system, this supports the phonetic relationship. It does not establish a name or pronunciation for any object depicted by 尚, nor is a whole-graph loan required by its role as a sound component.
evidence.title: 尚 - Wiktionary

evidence.text: The Commons page describes 常-seal.svg as a vector rendering of 常 in Shuowen seal-script style and lists Sinica, Chinese Etymology, CUHK, Ctext, and Chinese Linguipedia among available source references. The page explicitly releases the SVG representation into the public domain. This is a modern digital drawing, not an ancient artifact photograph.

search_audit.outcome: Opened both entries and inspected modern readings and Middle Chinese, Baxter–Sagart, and Zhengzhang tables. The Zhengzhang level-tone reconstructions match at *djaŋ; 尚 also has a distinct departing-tone reading *djaŋs.

search_audit.outcome: Clicked the Commons page's other-version links; they led to general script categories, not 常-specific media. Direct guessed 常-bronze and 常- Chu file URLs failed to open and are not proposed.

gaps: No inspected source established a Shang oracle-bone form for 常. The consulted databases report bronze, Warring States, Chu manuscript, small-seal, or received Shuowen material, but available page text did not establish a first attestation date.

The clothing sense is reported in named bronze and Warring States examples, but the inspected references do not date those artifacts or establish which is earliest. No primary inscription image was inspected.

The garment-to-‘constant/custom/frequent’ semantic path is not fully dated. Sources assert phonetic borrowing or extension; the reported bronze custom/law use shows early non-garment usage but does not itself explain the semantic transition.

CUHK reports a competing view attributed to 朱駿聲 that 常 originally meant a flag and 裳 the garment. CUHK argues bronze clothing examples weigh against it; the primary inscription images were not inspected, so the dispute is recorded rather than independently adjudicated.
CUHK reports ancient mixing of 常 and 嘗 that diminished after the Ming and Qing; the consulted source does not establish that 常 itself arose by corruption. No specific corruption claim is supported.
No direct evidence located for a whole-graph loan of garment 常 to an unrelated spoken word. Evidence supports a phonetic-compound analysis with 尚 as sound component; these are distinct claims.

The identification of 巾 as the clothing-related semantic element and 尚 as phonetic is supported by the inspected specialist sources. 尚's own earliest depicted referent has competing interpretations and is not resolved here; this uncertainty does not negate its independently supported later phonetic role.

No 常-specific reusable bronze or Chu manuscript image was established from the searches. Direct candidate URLs failed or led to category pages; the sole proposed glyph is a modern seal-script vector redraw with explicit public-domain provenance.
The Commons page provides source references for the seal drawing but the linked underlying glyph image itself could not be opened through the browser tool. No pixel-level inspection is claimed.

items.period: Shuowen seal-script style; associated with the received Han-dynasty Shuowen tradition, exact glyph exemplar date not specified
items.caption: A modern vector rendering of 常 in Shuowen seal-script style. The cited historical analysis parses the lower part as 巾 and the upper 尚 as phonetic.
items.alt: Black seal-script rendering of 常 with a compact upper 尚-like section above a lower 巾-like section.
items.selection_reason: The only 常-specific candidate found with inspected source and reuse statements; its form usefully presents the component arrangement cited in the historical account.
items.rights: Commons page states the SVG representation is public domain and that the creator released any copyright in the digital rendering.

limitations.text: This is a modern digital redrawing of a historical script form, not a photograph or facsimile of an ancient object. The browser inspection covered the description/provenance page; it did not inspect the image pixels.

Searches did not establish Commons files specifically for 常 in bronze or Chu manuscript styles. The opened additional-version links led to general script categories, and direct guessed URLs were inaccessible; no such image is proposed.
